title: The Density Illusion
excerpt: Why Apple's A14 exposed the gap between theoretical transistor density and real chip density, and why AI-era scaling now depends on SRAM, memory bandwidth, packaging, power, and architecture. Moore's Law did not die. It became a system problem.

title: The Modem-to-Antenna War
excerpt: How Apple is taking apart Qualcomm's modem-RF moat, from the iPhone 12 mmWave antenna decision to the Apple C1 modem. Qualcomm still has the best complete engine. Apple is trying to own the car.

title: Nvidia Didn't Buy Arm. It Built the AI Factory Anyway.
excerpt: How Nvidia failed to buy Arm but still built the CPU-GPU-DPU-networking-software stack behind the modern AI factory. The acquisition failed. The strategy did not.

title: MediaTek and the Fragmented Compute War
excerpt: How MediaTek moved from Huawei-substitution thesis to a broader role in flagship phones, edge AI, automotive platforms, and custom data-center ASICs. In 2020, the question was who supplies Huawei. In 2026, the question is who supplies compute.

title: The Dry Resist War
excerpt: Why Lam's Aether dry resist matters for EUV, High-NA lithography, DRAM, HBM, and AI-era chipmaking. EUV exposed the wafer. The resist has to do the rest.

title: The AI Memory Wall
excerpt: Why DRAM, HBM, advanced packaging, and semicap became central to the AI infrastructure race. The AI boom is usually described as a GPU shortage. That is only half true. The deeper bottleneck is memory.

title: The Prompt Is Not Infrastructure
excerpt: Prompts are instructions, not controls. As AI agents gain access to tools, private data, and external actions, trustworthy AI will require permissions, sandboxes, logs, and real infrastructure.

title: The Interface Coup
excerpt: AI will not merely replace search. It may replace the interface layer. When assistants become the front door, apps become callable infrastructure and distribution moves from visibility to permission.

title: The Memory Moat
excerpt: The next AI moat may not be the best model. It may be memory: the accumulated context that makes an assistant feel like it knows you. When AI remembers who you are becoming, switching tools becomes harder.

title: The Model Monoculture
excerpt: What happens when millions of people think, write, code, research, and decide through the same few AI models? The danger is not only wrong answers. It is correlated cognition.

title: Liability Laundering
excerpt: AI agents will not just answer questions. They will act across systems, tools, data, and customers. The hidden danger is liability laundering: humans remain responsible while practical control moves elsewhere.

title: The Free Intelligence Trap
excerpt: Free AI is not just the next ad-supported product. Search monetized what people wanted. Social monetized who they were. AI may monetize the moment before they decide.

title: The Cheap Code Era
excerpt: AI will automate coding before it can own software. The cheap code era is here, but the expensive part of software is moving from syntax to systems, judgment, verification, security, and accountability.

title: Yann LeCun's Billion-Dollar Bet: Intelligence Beyond the Next Token
excerpt: LeCun's argument is not that LLMs are useless. It is that real intelligence may require world models that predict consequences, plan actions, and understand reality beyond text.

title: The Boiling Frog Economy
excerpt: How AI quietly breaks the ladder before it breaks the job market. The danger is not that some jobs disappear. It is that the first rung disappears first.

title: The title was wrong. That's what made it historic.
excerpt: Everyone remembers 'Attention Is All You Need' as the attention paper. The real innovation was something later summaries under-emphasized, and it explains everything that came after.

title: There is no Alexander without Aristotle
excerpt: On intelligence as infrastructure, why the education system was never designed for you, and what it took to understand the world on my own terms.
